planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in spring in full sun on lean, well-drained soil; this selection tolerates drought, wind, salt spray, and poor alkaline ground once established.

directions: Quicksilver is a named selection of Russian olive prized for its exceptionally narrow, intensely silver-white leaves that give the small tree a shimmering, almost metallic look from a distance. Like the species it fixes nitrogen through root nodules, flowers with small fragrant creamy-yellow blooms in late spring, and sets small yellow-dusted silvery fruit that is edible fresh or dried though mealy and mildly sweet rather than juicy. It is outstandingly tough in dry, windy, coastal, or alkaline sites and makes a fine specimen or windbreak tree, but check local invasive-species restrictions before planting since the species self-sows readily in parts of the western and northern United States. Prune lightly after flowering to shape, since old wood tolerates hard cutting back if the tree becomes leggy.

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring in full sun to light shade on well-drained soil; cut out any plain-green reversion shoots promptly to preserve the gold variegation.

directions: Dicksonii is one of the oldest named selections of thorny elaeagnus, bearing broad evergreen leaves with a bold central splash of deep gold that is larger and coarser than the variegation on the better-known 'Maculata'. Small, intensely fragrant, creamy-white flowers open in autumn and are followed by tart, edible red berries the following spring, and like the species it fixes nitrogen and tolerates drought, salt spray, wind, and poor or alkaline soils once established. Grow it as an accent shrub or informal hedge where its coarse golden foliage can be appreciated up close, and shear lightly after flowering if a tidier shape is wanted. Give it full sun for the richest gold coloring, since shadier sites cause the variegation to fade and encourage reversion to plain green growth.
sources: Hillier Manual of Trees and Shrubs
